voice.name: Liam
voice.note: New v4 Liam narration. No v3 files were overwritten. Word times come from the ElevenLabs with-timestamps alignment.

scenes.vo: You know the pothole. The one everyone swerves. The one nobody owns. It has been there for months. This morning, it nearly takes out a cyclist. So you stop. You take one photo. And you decide this little patch of street gets fixed. Not by waiting. By starting.
scenes.caption:
You know the pothole.
Everyone swerves. Nobody owns it.

scenes.vo: A pothole photo can carry GPS, a timestamp, your home route, your kid's school, even a plate. So MEND cleans it in your browser first. EXIF and GPS are gone before anything leaves your phone. Think of the AI as a private tutor. It reads only the cleaned note. It flags duplicates and drafts a scope. That is all. No wallet. No approval button. No payment authority. A steward confirms the merge. Two neighbors reported it, so one case moves forward. Humans decide. Fastify and Postgres are the town clerk and the ledger.
scenes.caption:
Your photo. Your privacy.
EXIF + GPS erased before upload.

scenes.vo: Next, a steward sets the scope and a maximum budget. Then a real Sputnik DAO votes. Two of three council members. Not the AI. The budget, roster and scoring policy become public rules. A committee in the open, with a receipt for every decision. The money waits in a Rust escrow: a lockbox that opens only when the rules are met.
scenes.caption:
Steward proposes.
Sputnik DAO: 2 of 3 humans approve.

scenes.vo: Three contractors submit sealed bids. When the window closes, a referee runs one hash-pinned rule. Price, warranty, duration, materials. Same rule for everyone. No language model picks the winner. Bid B wins on total value, not the cheapest sticker. That referee is OutLayer. You can check the score. You can check the policy.
scenes.caption:
Sealed bids. One referee.
B wins on total value, not sticker price.

scenes.vo: The repair is physical. Clean, fill, compact, seal. Every photo and note is hashed onto the work order. Then a different human shows up. Not the contractor. Not the AI. An outside inspector with a checklist, evidence and a signature. The lockbox pays only after that signature.
scenes.caption:
A different human inspects.
Checklist. Evidence. Signature.

scenes.vo: On acceptance, the escrow splits exactly. One hundred funded. Twenty refunded at award. Seventy-two paid to the contractor. Eight held for durability. One hundred, twenty, seventy-two, eight. The job is done. The community keeps leverage. A later durability pass releases the last eight. Escrow ends at zero.
scenes.caption:
100 funded · 20 refunded
72 paid · 8 held · escrow 0

scenes.vo: Now the repair has a memory. The pothole gets a passport: a permanent report card owned by the work order, not a platform. If the repair fails, you reopen the same case. Same history. No new bounty. No new money. The failure stays attached.
scenes.caption:
Same work order. Same history.
No new bounty. No new money.

scenes.vo: Under the hood, it's a neighborhood. Next.js and React are the front door. Fastify and Postgres are the town clerk. NEAR AI is the private tutor. Rust escrow is the lockbox. Sputnik is the committee. OutLayer is the referee. NEP-366 is the free stamp. Agent Market is the outside inspector. The V2 run recorded 42 transactions. The pothole story is replay; the rails are real. Every payment and vote has a receipt.
scenes.caption:
REPLAY / SIMULATION story.
Real NEAR testnet rails · 42 tx

scenes.vo: That is MEND. Maintenance with memory. You report it. Humans decide. The contract enforces. The neighborhood remembers. Try the live demo at mend-demo.vercel.app. Get it fixed. Keep it fixed.
scenes.caption:
MEND — maintenance with memory.
mend-demo.vercel.app
